meta.title: Robustness at Scale: tables, claims and re-estimations
meta.tagline: The regression tables, the claims and the re-estimated values of the same papers, three linked datasets, one process: uploaded from the pipeline, checked against each other, the headline columns and the reproduction verdicts written on the tables, reviewed paper by paper, released together.
meta.description: One workflow over three datasets of the Robustness-at-Scale pipeline: every new paper's tables, claims and re-estimation files enter the group together with its PDF; each side is re-checked against its contract, the printed cells against each other, the cited estimates against the paper's own tables; then two deterministic steps write on the tables what the other two sides say about each column — whether a main estimate of a stated claim links to it (a headline result), and how its re-estimation from the deposited code graded at printed precision — and a joint review walks both sides of each paper before the datasets are released as one. Everything that needs the replication package, Stata or a sandboxed agent (the data check, the workspace, the re-estimation, the provenance) runs in the pipeline; Metalens holds its outputs and puts the hand decisions in front of reviewers.

authors.affiliation: University of Basel; University of Copenhagen

steps.label: Regression tables
steps.help: one entry per estimated column, transcribed by the pipeline outside Metalens (metalens/sync/export.py) and uploaded here with the PDF; the headline and reproduction fields stay empty until the compute steps fill them

steps.label: Claims and their results
steps.help: the claims the paper states and the results that carry them, transcribed by the pipeline and uploaded with the same PDF

steps.label: Re-estimated regressions
steps.help: what the re-estimation agent got when it ran the deposited code for each regression of the blinded grid (reproduce/<artid>.result.json), uploaded with the same PDF; a paper the pipeline did not re-estimate has no file here

steps.label: Number check
steps.help: every standard error names its coefficient, the parsed number is the printed one, stars agree with the level and the p-value, t with coefficient over se, the stated N with the printed N

steps.label: Estimates against the tables
steps.help: each cited point estimate against the coefficient cells of the same paper's tables (the group's tables dataset); a resolved column with no matching cell is an error, an exhibit no column matches a warning

steps.label: Headline regressions
steps.help: the claim chain's rule, deterministic: a regression column is a headline result when at least one main estimate of a stated claim (an edge or a comparison) links to it; written on each column with the claims it carries and whether the text points to it; a main result that names no column of the tables is a finding

steps.label: Grade the re-estimation
steps.help: the pipeline's grading, deterministic: every withheld cell of a column against its reproduced value at half the last printed digit, sign never ignored, a whole-paper rescaling by a power of ten detected and recorded; one verdict per column (match, partial, mismatch, sign_flip, failed, not_attempted, not_returned), the paper's match rate, and a finding per cell that did not reproduce

steps.label: Joint review
steps.help: every new paper on both sides: its regression columns with their headline and reproduction verdicts, then its claims with their verdicts against the tables, in one worklist

steps.label: Sign flips
steps.help: a paper whose re-estimation reproduced a value at the right size with the wrong sign: a person decides whether the published table, the transcription or the re-estimation is wrong; never holds the release
